ecomOS Workflows
Draft for Kevin, 25 Sep 2026

Each agent is a new hire with a written way of working and a shelf of skills.

A workflow is the predetermined procedure for one job, the way a good person in the role would do it. A skill is a reusable step, nested so the agent picks the right sub-skill for the format, channel or platform. The Orchestrator hands a card to the owning agent with the workflow id; the agent follows the steps and loads skills as it goes.

Paid creative and copy · CREA-W01

Launch a new paid creative test, start to finish

Read it as a new hire's first week: each step says what they do, what comes out, what they check, and which skill they pull off the shelf. Skills light up on the right.

1
Pull the objection map and format scan

Pulls the brand's existing mined research (voice of customer, owned by the Brand Brain Keeper) plus a fresh check of the account's own last 90 days of ad-level results for which formats currently deliver best (hook rate, hold rate, CPA by format).

Out objection map (each objection quoted and sourced) plus a format scan citing real numbersCheck every objection has a quoted source and a date; every 'format working now' line cites a real metric, not an impression
crea/research/objection-and-format-scan

a new test needs its research pulled fresh before angles can be written

script: intelligence/creative_retrieval.pymcp: Meta_MCP ads_insights_performance_trend (read)
2
Pull competitor signal for layout and mood

Pulls 3 to 8 competitor ad references from the Meta gallery's Competitors tab and the Reference Scout, tagged with why each fits this bottleneck.

Out 3 to 8 tagged competitor references, layout and mood onlyCheck every reference carries a one-line reason and a 'signal only' tag; no text, logo, product or face is marked for reuse
crea/research/competitor-signal-pull

a workflow step needs layout or mood references from competitor ads, never their text, logo, product or face

meta_gallery: Competitors tabmcp: Meta_MCP ads_library_search (read)
3
Define the angle and dominant appeal

Turns the objection map, format scan and avatar into 2 to 4 candidate angles, each one sentence, one persona, one dominant appeal, one buying question.

Out angle brief: 2 to 4 angles, each with persona, appeal, buying question, awareness stageCheck no angle uses a forbidden-tier claim; each angle names one dominant appeal only
crea/angle-and-test/angle-builder

a research packet exists and a small set of testable angles needs to be defined before any copy is written

script: scripts/search_knowledge.py --keyword-only
4
Write the test plan

Turns the angle brief into a hypothesis, a clean one-persona-per-ad-set structure, a pack size sized to the account's own delivery volume, and a pre-set winner and kill rule for the creative side.

Out test brief: hypothesis, pack size, winner rule, kill rule, minimum read windowCheck winner and kill rule exist before any script is written; pack size matches this account's real traffic, not a generic default
crea/angle-and-test/test-plan-builder

an angle brief is ready and the creative side of a test needs a hypothesis, pack size and pre-set win/kill rule

5
Build the audience spec and hand it to MEDIA

Turns the angle's persona into age range, traits, interests and exclusions matched to the avatar record, and hands the spec to the Media buyer specialist as a structured request. CREA does not build or launch the audience itself.

Out audience spec record: age range, traits, exclusions, matched persona id, handed to MEDIACheck every trait in the spec ties back to a line in the persona record, not a guess
crea/angle-and-test/audience-spec-handoff

an angle's persona needs to become a concrete targeting spec and be handed to the Media buyer, without CREA building or launching it

6
Pick the format and compare format economics

Chooses the ad format (static, native platform format, UGC video, founder video, carousel, catalogue) from the product's real education or demo need and the account's own expected profit per ad by format, not ROAS alone.

Out format decision with the profit-per-ad comparison behind itCheck decision cites a number, not a preference
crea/angle-and-test/format-economics

a concept is set and the ad format still needs choosing, compared by expected profit per ad rather than ROAS alone

7
Write hooks and scripts or copy per format

Writes the hook bank (8 to 20 hooks, graded on 5 criteria) and the format-specific script or static copy structure for each chosen format.

Out hook bank plus a script or copy draft per formatCheck no product name or offer in a cold hook; one dominant appeal held throughout
crea/write-copy/hooks

the copy needed is the opening line or opening 3 seconds of a cold video, VSL or static, before any full script is written

meta_gallery lab: ENGINE.adDetail (past hook performance)
8
Build the creative brief and production or shoot brief

Fills the one-page concept brief, then the format-specific production brief (static design brief, UGC or founder-video brief, or catalogue template spec) and generates a first draft image where the format calls for one.

Out concept brief, production brief, and a draft asset (image or script package)Check destination link matches the offer stated; hook, image and copy share one awareness stage; real product photo used if fit, material or scale matters
crea/briefing/concept-brief

an idea is approved and the fixed one-page brief must exist before any design tool or shoot is booked

meta_gallery studio: /api/variantsmeta_gallery studio: /api/competitor-variants
9
Run the copy and claim-compliance pass

Applies the fixed direct-response copywriting rules (reading level, single idea, proof ranking) and then the brand's claim-tier and platform-policy check on every line.

Out edited copy plus a claim audit table, pass or fail per lineCheck reading level under grade 10; no claim from the forbidden tier; no em dash
crea/compliance/copy-craft-rules

any drafted copy needs the account's fixed direct-response writing rules applied before the claim-tier check

10
Run a feedback and reference round with the Reference Scout

Sends the draft brief and asset back through one reference round: checks it against the tagged competitor references for layout and mood fit, and routes it for one internal feedback pass before it reaches a human reviewer.

Out revised brief or asset with a short note on what changed and whyCheck no competitor text, logo, product or face was copied in the revision
judgement step, no skill
11
Apply naming and tagging

Applies the fixed naming and tagging schema (concept, persona, angle, offer, format, stage, source) to every asset and copy file before it leaves CREA.

Out named, tagged asset setCheck every asset has a stable id following the current schema
crea/production-ops/naming-and-tagging

any asset needs a stable id and tags, or the platform-spec sheet or schema needs its periodic refresh

12
Build the launch checklist and hand off to MEDIA

Assembles the launch checklist (creative files, copy, audience spec reference, test brief, destination link, tracking check) and hands the full package to the Media buyer specialist for account build and go-live.

Out launch checklist and handoff package to MEDIACheck every checklist line is checked or has a named blocker; MEDIA confirms receipt
judgement step, no skill
13
Read the first-read numbers

At the test brief's minimum read window, pulls the creative-side metrics (hook rate, hold rate, CPA per ad) from the metric contract and compares each ad to the account average and the test's pre-set winner and kill rule.

Out read note: winner, loser or inconclusive, per ad, against the pre-set ruleCheck verdict uses the pre-set rule, not a new judgment call; missing metrics show as unavailable, never zero
judgement step, no skill
14
Log the result and close the loop

Writes the registry entry for this test (angle, format, hook, result, learning) so the next research pass in step 1 starts from it.

Out registry entryCheck entry links back to the original card or idea id
shared/registry-entry
Workflows

Every job, as a numbered procedure.

Open a workflow to read its steps: what the agent does, the skill it pulls, the tools, the output, the check, and when it stops to ask the founder.

ORCH-W01Onboard a brand through Door Bevent: new brand added with a website · 6 steps

As a person would call it: account manager onboarding a client. Needs: website URL, founder contact, door and approval chain defaults. Capabilities: ORCH-C08.

  1. 1
    Read the site

    Run BRN-W01 steps 2 and 3 for the first time: full crawl, snapshot, claims tiered as site-backed, first speed run.

    brn/site-diffscript: crawlerscript: speed_lab
    Out brand record v0, first speed measurementCheck products, policies and claims each have a page source
  2. 2
    Connect sources

    Present the connector list. For each granted source run the collector and compute the contract fields it enables.

    no skill, judgementconnectors
    Out connections with status, contract partialCheck ungranted sources show as unavailable with a connect cardAsk founder if a source needs a grant only the founder can give
  3. 3
    Ingest documents and notes

    Extract facts with sources from Drive, Notion and uploads. Raise conflicts with the site.

    brn/document-extractmcp: google drivemcp: notion
    Out facts, conflictsCheck a summary is not a fact
  4. 4
    Interview rounds

    Ask what data cannot answer: margins, what was tried, competitors as the founder sees them, red lines, real policies. Store answers as decisions.

    shared/founder-question-round
    Out decisions log entriesCheck no question the brain can already answerAsk founder if always; this step is the founder
  5. 5
    First break and top 10

    Run DIAG-W01 and PROP-W01 on what is readable. Show the Today screen with unavailable stages named.

    no skill, judgement

  6. 6

Outputs: brand brain v1, connections, Today screen, roles. QA before the gate: every fact has a source; no external write happened. Read point: 28 days: brain health and first reads. Duration: 1 day of agent time spread over the founder's answers.

Diagnose DIAG · 1 workflows

DIAG-W01Find the breakscheduled daily after BRN-W01 · 4 steps

As a person would call it: business analyst running the morning numbers. Needs: contract values and 4 trailing windows, store tags, benchmarks by store type, founder goal for the period. Capabilities: DIAG-C01, DIAG-C02, DIAG-C03.

  1. 1
    Compute deltas and stake

    In code: current vs own trailing median vs peer band per pipeline stage, and money at stake per stage.

    shared/metric-readscript: contract.compute_deltas
    Out delta tableCheck every row has a window ending on a full day
  2. 2
    Rank the breaks

    Sort stages by stake, tie-break by confidence then upstream position. Unreadable stages listed separately.

    diag/break-rankingcode
    Out ranked breaks, unreadable listCheck an unreadable stage is never marked healthy
  3. 3
    Write the proof

    For the top 3 breaks, the numbers, the window, what changed and since when. No fix words.

    diag/break-proof
    Out proof linesCheck every number quoted is in the delta tableAsk founder if two breaks tie and the numbers cannot settle it
  4. 4
    Founder line

    One sentence naming the break, one on why it is first, one on the next in line.

    shared/plain-english-card
    Out founder_line, next_break_lineCheck reading level under grade 10

Outputs: breaks[], unreadable[], founder lines. QA before the gate: no fix language; windows on full days. Read point: none. Duration: 2 minutes.

Propose PROP · 1 workflows

PROP-W01Build the top 10 for a breakscheduled daily after DIAG-W01, or on demand for a chosen break · 7 steps

As a person would call it: head of growth prioritising the week. Needs: the break with proof, store tags, red lines, registry exclusions and priors, reach numbers for the stage. Capabilities: PROP-C01, PROP-C02, PROP-C03, PROP-C05, PROP-C06, PROP-C07.

  1. 1
    Audit the surface

    Dispatch the surface auditor for this break. Speed: the lab on 3 pages. Conversion: funnel pages and checkout. Retention: flows and order gaps. Paid: structure and results.

    shared/surface-auditscript: speed_labscript: crawlermcp: ad accounts (read)mcp: email platform (read)
    Out observed conditions with evidenceCheck every condition has evidence a person can verifyAsk founder if the audit needs an access grant
  2. 2
    Filter the bank

    In code: ideas by bottleneck and store tags, minus exclusions with a live reason.

    no skill, judgementscript: scripts/ideas.py
    Out candidate ideasCheck no excluded idea present
  3. 3
    Match signals

    Batches of 40: does each idea's signal fire on the observed conditions, with the quote.

    prop/signal-match
    Out fired ideas with evidenceCheck every fired idea quotes a condition
  4. 4
    Web pass

    Verify time-sensitive claims and search for tactics the bank lacks, within the budget. New candidates to the candidates file.

    shared/web-research-budgetedweb search and fetch
    Out facts and candidates with URL and dateCheck budget not exceeded; every fact dated
  5. 5
    Fill evidence fields and rank

    Reach from the contract, effect basis from the record or source, brand prior from the registry, effort, cost, risk, dependencies, founder weight. Then the code sort.

    shared/rank-candidatesscript: intelligence/ideas.py rank
    Out ranked list with score partsCheck source carries no weight
  6. 6
    Challenge the top 15

    Re-check each against the audit. Demote weak signals and overstated effects with a one-line reason. Promote stronger audit or web ideas.

    prop/challenge-idea
    Out final order, demoted[]Check every change from the code sort is written downAsk founder if two strong cards conflict
  7. 7
    Write the cards

    Top 10 as plain-English cards with metric, read point, stop rule, owner specialist and workflow id from the routing table.

    shared/plain-english-card
    Out cards[]Check every card names an observed condition and a read point

Outputs: cards[], demoted[], candidates file entries. QA before the gate: no card crosses a red line or a live exclusion; effect sizes from the record or a dated source only. Read point: per card, at its read point. Duration: 20 to 40 minutes, mostly sub-agents.

Registrar REG · 1 workflows

REG-W01Take a readevent: a registry entry reaches its read point · 4 steps

As a person would call it: analyst closing an experiment. Needs: the entry with metric, window, kill and scale rule, contract at read time. Capabilities: REG-C02, REG-C03, REG-C04, REG-C06.

  1. 1
    Read the metric

    Pull the metric for the entry's window. Early or unavailable is recorded as such, never as a result.

    shared/metric-readscript: contract
    Out value with windowCheck window matches the rule
  2. 2
    Compare to the rule

    In code: up, down, flat, or unreadable against the kill and scale rule.

    no skill, judgementcode
    Out resultCheck no result without a full window
  3. 3
    Write the learning

    One plain sentence with the number. Update the brand's prior for the idea. If agency-run and not opted out, update the overlay with direction and tags only.

    reg/learning-line
    Out learning line, prior update, overlay rowCheck overlay carries no brand identity
  4. 4
    Notify

    Tell the Orchestrator so the Today screen and the weekly review pick it up.

    no skill, judgement
    Out eventCheck

Outputs: read result, learning line, prior update. QA before the gate: every result quotes the window. Read point: this is the read. Duration: 1 minute.

QA-W01Gate an artefactevent: a card, artefact or report is ready · 4 steps

As a person would call it: editor and compliance reviewer. Needs: the artefact, claims tiers, prices and policies, voice examples and forbidden words, contract fields cited, write-permission table, competitor text corpus. Capabilities: QA-C01, LOOP-C12, LOOP-C12, QA-C07.

    no skill, judgement

Outputs: pass or failures[], warnings[]. QA before the gate: the gate never edits; it returns. Read point: none. Duration: 2 to 5 minutes.

Brand Brain Keeper BRN · 1 workflows

BRN-W01Daily collection, crawl and contractscheduled daily 04:00 · 6 steps

As a person would call it: data analyst and site auditor. Needs: connector list with access levels, last site snapshot, claims tiers. Capabilities: BRN-C01, BRN-C02, BRN-C03, BRN-C05, BRN-C06.

    Run collectors

    Pull orders, sessions, spend, flows, tickets, reviews and competitor snapshots for yesterday. Stamp each pull.

    no skill, judgement

Outputs: warehouse rows, change log, open questions, contract values, brain health. QA before the gate: every fact has a source and a date; no section claims high confidence with an unavailable input. Read point: none; this is the data step. Duration: 15 minutes of scripts, no waiting.

Site SITE · 30 workflows

SITE-W01Choose the platform, stand up the account and secure the domainon demand · 9 steps

As a person would call it: New store setup lead. Needs: brand brain: budget and team capacity, brand brain: catalogue size and SKU complexity, brand brain: legal entity, founder decision log. Capabilities: SITE-C01, SITE-C02, SITE-C03.

  1. 1
    List required features before comparing platforms

    Reads catalogue size, SKU complexity, budget and design needs and turns them into a written feature list before looking at any platform.

    site/store-setup-checklistscript: scripts/ideas.py
    Out feature requirement listCheck Every item on the list ties to a real product or catalogue fact, not a guess.
  2. 2
    Score total cost of ownership

    Scores hosting, apps, transaction fees and developer time as one true yearly cost per platform (Shopify, WooCommerce, custom), not the sticker price.

    site/store-setup-checklistweb search
    Out cost comparison tableCheck Every cost line carries a source and a date.
  3. 3
    Recommend platform and plan tier

    Picks the platform and plan tier with the lowest true cost, and names the exact trigger (order volume, feature need) that should force an upgrade.

    site/store-setup-checklist
    Out platform recommendation memoCheck The memo states a numeric upgrade trigger, not a vague 'when you grow'.Ask founder if budget or catalogue size has not been confirmed with the founder
  4. 4
    Register the account and enter legal identity

    Registers under an email the business permanently controls and enters the exact legal identity before any payment or tax setting is touched.

    site/store-setup-checklistmcp: shopifyconnector: woocommerce admin
    Out setup checklist entriesCheck Account email is a business domain address, not a personal inbox.
  5. 5
    Set defaults and turn on account security

    Sets currency, region and unit defaults once, before any price is entered, and turns on two-factor authentication before payments are activated.

    no skill, judgement
    Out security configuration reportCheck 2FA confirmed on before any gateway is touched, checked live not from a settings screenshot.
  6. 6
    Set staff roles and time-bound agency access

    Creates custom staff roles and gives any agency collaborator access that expires on a set date rather than standing forever.

    no skill, judgement
    Out security configuration reportCheck No collaborator has owner-level access without an end date.Ask founder if an agency needs standing access beyond the current project
  7. 7
    Buy the domain and avoid the platform default

    Filters candidate names by brandability, buys the real domain and never launches on the platform's default subdomain.

    no skill, judgementconnector: dnsweb search
    Out DNS change listCheck The live storefront never resolves to a *.myshopify.com or platform default URL.
  8. 8
    Point DNS for the platform and for sender authentication

    Points DNS at the platform and reuses the same DNS workflow to add SPF, DKIM and DMARC records for sender domain authentication.

    no skill, judgement
    Out DNS change listCheck Every DNS record is verified resolving live, not just saved in the registrar panel.
  9. 9
    Register near-miss domains and matching TLDs

    Registers the near-miss spellings and additional TLDs a squatter would use to imitate the brand.

    no skill, judgement
    Out domain readiness reportCheck Registrar choice favors portability over convenience unless there is a real reason not to.Ask founder if budget is tight and squatting risk is genuinely low for this category

Outputs: platform recommendation memo, cost comparison table, setup checklist, security configuration report, DNS change list, domain readiness report. QA before the gate: Every claim and number traces to the brand record or a dated web source.; 2FA is on before payments are touched.; No leftover agency access without an end date.; DNS verified live, not just saved.. Read point: Kevin reviews the memo and checklist before any payment is set live; DNS re-checked 24-48h after propagation.. Duration: agent: 2-3 hours across the three capabilities; waiting: up to 48 hours for DNS propagation and domain registration confirmation..

SITE-W02Select the theme and put safe engineering practice behind iton demand | store setup, or after a near-miss where a live edit could not be traced or reverted · 10 steps

As a person would call it: Theme developer / engineering lead. Needs: brand brain: required PDP/collection features, founder decision log, GitHub repo access or Shopify CLI. Capabilities: SITE-C04, SITE-C05, SITE-C62, SITE-C69, SITE-C70.

  1. 1
    List required sections and features

    Writes the list of sections and features a theme must have before browsing any theme store.

    site/theme-engineering
    Out feature requirement listCheck List is written before a single theme is opened.
  2. 2
    Vet 2-3 candidate themes

    Vets each candidate on PDP quality, mobile behaviour and code quality, not the homepage demo, and scores each against the feature list.

    site/theme-engineeringbrowser: headless chromiummcp: shopify
    Out theme shortlist with scoresCheck Every theme is checked on a real PDP and a real mobile width, not the marketplace preview.
  3. 3
    Decide free vs paid and pick one

    Picks the theme with the best fit-to-cost, not the best looking demo.

    no skill, judgement
    Out theme decision memoCheck Decision states the runner-up and why it lost.Ask founder if two themes score within 5% and cost differs materially
  4. 4
    Duplicate the theme before any edit round

    Never edits the live theme directly; every change round starts on a duplicate or a branch.

    site/theme-pr-diff
    Out duplicate theme / branchCheck The live theme's edit history shows zero direct edits.
  5. 5
    Stand up git, CI and a staging theme

    Connects the theme repo to GitHub, adds Shopify CLI for local development, runs theme-check linting on every commit, and builds a staging theme URL that auto-deploys from a branch.

    site/theme-engineering/git-ci-pipelinemcp: github
    Out git repo with commit history, CI config, staging theme URLCheck A commit with a hard theme-check error is blocked from merging.
  6. 6
    Write the AI build brief before any AI agent touches the storefront

    Gives the build agent real brand inputs (products, policy, voice), lets it propose a plan first, and asks for exactly one storefront change per prompt.

    site/theme-engineering/ai-build-guardrail
    Out AI build briefCheck The brief is written and approved before the agent makes its first live edit.
  7. 7
    Preview privately and QA every AI-authored section

    Previews every AI-built section privately, never on the public URL, and treats the output as a draft needing manual QA and a claims check.

    shared/claim-checkbrowser: headless chromium
    Out QA pass reportCheck No AI-authored copy ships without a claim-check pass.
  8. 8
    Require review before merge and keep a tested rollback

    Requires a second reviewer or the founder gate before merging staging to the live theme, and keeps a one-command rollback to the previous release.

    site/theme-engineering/git-ci-pipeline
    Out change log, rollback runbookCheck Rollback has actually been run once in a drill, not just documented.
  9. 9
    Document design tokens and check new sections against them

    Documents color, spacing, typography and component tokens from the live theme, then checks every new section against them and flags drift.

    no skill, judgement
    Out design token doc, drift flagsCheck A new section that doesn't match a token is flagged before it ships, not after.
  10. 10
    Maintain a staging environment with real-looking data

    Keeps a staging copy of the store, theme and a recent product/price snapshot in sync with production, refreshed on a schedule, for every risky change or app trial.

    no skill, judgementstore_sync.mirror
    Out staging store, refresh scheduleCheck Every app trial and AI build-agent session runs against staging, never production.

Outputs: theme shortlist with scores, git repo with commit history + CI config, AI build brief, QA pass report, design token doc, staging store + refresh schedule, rollback runbook. QA before the gate: No edit ever lands on the live theme without a duplicate/branch and a reviewed PR.; Rollback command tested, not assumed.; AI-authored copy passed claim-check before merge.; New sections checked against the design token doc.. Read point: Founder reviews the PR before merge; token drift checked at every new section's QA.. Duration: agent: 1-2 days for initial engineering setup; ongoing: 30-60 minutes per theme change afterward..

Paid creative and copy CREA · 25 workflows

CREA-W01Launch a new paid creative test, start to finishan approved card from Propose | on demand · 14 steps

As a person would call it: Performance creative lead running one test from research to the first read. Needs: brand brain: voice, audience avatars, claim tiers, product facts, approved idea/card record with bottleneck and expected effect, registry: past creative tests and learnings for this persona and angle, metric contract: hook_rate, cvr_overall, cpa, roas_blended, with freshness stamps, Reference Scout access for competitor and swipe material. Capabilities: CREA-C03, CREA-C04, CREA-C05, CREA-C06, CREA-C07, CREA-C08, CREA-C11, CREA-C19, CREA-C20, CREA-C22, CREA-C24, CREA-C26, CREA-C31.

  1. 1
    Pull the objection map and format scan

    Pulls the brand's existing mined research (voice of customer, owned by the Brand Brain Keeper) plus a fresh check of the account's own last 90 days of ad-level results for which formats currently deliver best (hook rate, hold rate, CPA by format).

    crea/research/objection-and-format-scanscript: intelligence/creative_retrieval.pymcp: Meta_MCP ads_insights_performance_trend (read)
    Out objection map (each objection quoted and sourced) plus a format scan citing real numbersCheck every objection has a quoted source and a date; every 'format working now' line cites a real metric, not an impressionAsk founder if no support inbox or review source is connected for this brand
  2. 2
    Pull competitor signal for layout and mood

    Pulls 3 to 8 competitor ad references from the Meta gallery's Competitors tab and the Reference Scout, tagged with why each fits this bottleneck.

    crea/research/competitor-signal-pullmeta_gallery: Competitors tabmcp: Meta_MCP ads_library_search (read)
    Out 3 to 8 tagged competitor references, layout and mood onlyCheck every reference carries a one-line reason and a 'signal only' tag; no text, logo, product or face is marked for reuse
  3. 3
    Define the angle and dominant appeal

    Turns the objection map, format scan and avatar into 2 to 4 candidate angles, each one sentence, one persona, one dominant appeal, one buying question.

    crea/angle-and-test/angle-builderscript: scripts/search_knowledge.py --keyword-only
    Out angle brief: 2 to 4 angles, each with persona, appeal, buying question, awareness stageCheck no angle uses a forbidden-tier claim; each angle names one dominant appeal only
  4. 4
    Write the test plan

    Turns the angle brief into a hypothesis, a clean one-persona-per-ad-set structure, a pack size sized to the account's own delivery volume, and a pre-set winner and kill rule for the creative side.

    crea/angle-and-test/test-plan-builder
    Out test brief: hypothesis, pack size, winner rule, kill rule, minimum read windowCheck winner and kill rule exist before any script is written; pack size matches this account's real traffic, not a generic default
  5. 5
    Build the audience spec and hand it to MEDIA

    Turns the angle's persona into age range, traits, interests and exclusions matched to the avatar record, and hands the spec to the Media buyer specialist as a structured request. CREA does not build or launch the audience itself.

    crea/angle-and-test/audience-spec-handoff
    Out audience spec record: age range, traits, exclusions, matched persona id, handed to MEDIACheck every trait in the spec ties back to a line in the persona record, not a guessAsk founder if the angle targets a persona with no avatar record yet
  6. 6
    Pick the format and compare format economics

    Chooses the ad format (static, native platform format, UGC video, founder video, carousel, catalogue) from the product's real education or demo need and the account's own expected profit per ad by format, not ROAS alone.

    crea/angle-and-test/format-economics
    Out format decision with the profit-per-ad comparison behind itCheck decision cites a number, not a preference
  7. 7
    Write hooks and scripts or copy per format

    Writes the hook bank (8 to 20 hooks, graded on 5 criteria) and the format-specific script or static copy structure for each chosen format.

    crea/write-copy/hooksmeta_gallery lab: ENGINE.adDetail (past hook performance)
    Out hook bank plus a script or copy draft per formatCheck no product name or offer in a cold hook; one dominant appeal held throughout
  8. 8
    Build the creative brief and production or shoot brief

    Fills the one-page concept brief, then the format-specific production brief (static design brief, UGC or founder-video brief, or catalogue template spec) and generates a first draft image where the format calls for one.

    crea/briefing/concept-briefmeta_gallery studio: /api/variantsmeta_gallery studio: /api/competitor-variants
    Out concept brief, production brief, and a draft asset (image or script package)Check destination link matches the offer stated; hook, image and copy share one awareness stage; real product photo used if fit, material or scale matters
  9. 9
    Run the copy and claim-compliance pass

    Applies the fixed direct-response copywriting rules (reading level, single idea, proof ranking) and then the brand's claim-tier and platform-policy check on every line.

    crea/compliance/copy-craft-rules
    Out edited copy plus a claim audit table, pass or fail per lineCheck reading level under grade 10; no claim from the forbidden tier; no em dashAsk founder if a claim sits at the edge of the site-backed tier
  10. 10
    Run a feedback and reference round with the Reference Scout

    Sends the draft brief and asset back through one reference round: checks it against the tagged competitor references for layout and mood fit, and routes it for one internal feedback pass before it reaches a human reviewer.

    no skill, judgement
    Out revised brief or asset with a short note on what changed and whyCheck no competitor text, logo, product or face was copied in the revision
  11. 11
    Apply naming and tagging

    Applies the fixed naming and tagging schema (concept, persona, angle, offer, format, stage, source) to every asset and copy file before it leaves CREA.

    crea/production-ops/naming-and-tagging
    Out named, tagged asset setCheck every asset has a stable id following the current schema
  12. 12
    Build the launch checklist and hand off to MEDIA

    Assembles the launch checklist (creative files, copy, audience spec reference, test brief, destination link, tracking check) and hands the full package to the Media buyer specialist for account build and go-live.

    no skill, judgement
    Out launch checklist and handoff package to MEDIACheck every checklist line is checked or has a named blocker; MEDIA confirms receipt
  13. 13
    Read the first-read numbers

    At the test brief's minimum read window, pulls the creative-side metrics (hook rate, hold rate, CPA per ad) from the metric contract and compares each ad to the account average and the test's pre-set winner and kill rule.

    no skill, judgement
    Out read note: winner, loser or inconclusive, per ad, against the pre-set ruleCheck verdict uses the pre-set rule, not a new judgment call; missing metrics show as unavailable, never zero
  14. 14
    Log the result and close the loop

    Writes the registry entry for this test (angle, format, hook, result, learning) so the next research pass in step 1 starts from it.

    shared/registry-entry
    Out registry entryCheck entry links back to the original card or idea id

Outputs: objection map, angle brief, test brief, audience spec record, hook bank, script or static copy, concept brief, production brief, draft asset, claim audit table, launch checklist, read note, registry entry. QA before the gate: every claim traced to an approved or site-backed tier; no competitor text, logo, product or face reused; reading level under grade 10; real product photo used where accuracy matters; winner and kill rule set before launch; every number came from the metric contract, not estimated. Read point: at the test brief's minimum read window (set in step 4 from the account's own delivery volume, not a fixed default). Duration: agent time: half a day to a day across the pipeline; waiting time: the read window itself, typically 3 to 10 days depending on account volume.

LIFE-W28Run the consumer-complaint and consumer-protection notice queueevent: grievance or notice received; weekly SLA check · 7 steps

As a person would call it: customer service / CX manager handling regulatory and consumer-protection complaints (BBB, state attorney general portals, FTC complaint referrals for the US; statutory grievance officer duties for India). Needs: complaint/notice inbox (BBB, state consumer-complaint portal, FTC referral for the US; grievance inbox for India), consumer-forum (e-Daakhil, India) and legal notice tracker, response SLA per channel (BBB and most state portals: about 2 weeks; India's E-Commerce Rules SLA of 48-hour acknowledgement and 1-month resolution, markets IN). Capabilities: LIFE-G03.

  1. 1
    Log every grievance on receipt

    Logs each BBB complaint, state consumer-complaint, FTC referral or legal notice (a grievance or e-Daakhil consumer-forum notice for India) the moment it arrives, with its own clock started from that timestamp.

    Out logged grievance with clock startedCheck clock starts from actual receipt, not from when it is read
  2. 2
    Acknowledge within the channel's SLA

    Sends the acknowledgement inside the SLA the receiving channel sets: BBB and most state consumer-complaint portals expect a response within about 2 weeks. India only: acknowledges within the 48-hour statutory window required under India's E-Commerce Rules instead; reads null for US brands.

    life/grievance-queueconnector: support platform (draft macro)
    Out acknowledgement sent with timestampCheck acknowledgement sent inside the applicable SLA (48 hours for India) or flagged as breached the moment it is missed
  3. 3
    Investigate and prepare the resolution

    Investigates the complaint against the order/product/policy record and prepares a resolution within the receiving channel's own window (India's 1-month statutory window; the target response time for a BBB or state consumer-complaint case in the US).

    life/grievance-queueconnector: shopify orders (read)brand brain (read)
    Out resolution draftCheck resolution draft cites the specific policy or order fact it rests on
  4. 4
    Track consumer-forum, BBB and legal notices separately

    Tracks any BBB case, state consumer-complaint case or legal notice (an e-Daakhil consumer-forum case for India) on its own separate clock and status, distinct from an ordinary grievance.

    life/grievance-queueweb search (budgeted)
    Out notice tracker updateCheck a legal notice is never merged into the ordinary complaint queue's SLA
  5. 5
    Run the weekly SLA check

    Checks every open complaint and notice against its own clock, flagging anything approaching or past deadline.

    life/grievance-queue
    Out weekly SLA reportCheck every open item shows days remaining or days breached, in code
  6. 6
    Route unresolved or escalated items to the founder

    Sends any item nearing breach, or any consumer-forum/legal notice, to the founder rather than letting its clock lapse quietly.

    shared/plain-english-card
    Out founder cardCheck an item nearing breach is never left for the next weekly check alone
  7. 7
    Log closure

    Records the resolution and closure date against the applicable deadline (statutory for India) once resolved.

    shared/registry-entry
    Out closure recordCheck closure date compared explicitly to the applicable deadline

Outputs: logged complaint/notice queue with SLA clocks, acknowledgements sent, resolution drafts, notice tracker, weekly SLA report. QA before the gate: acknowledgement and resolution windows tracked in code per channel (48-hour/1-month for India's statutory rule; each platform's own SLA for US channels); legal notices tracked on their own separate clock; nothing nearing breach left unescalated. Read point: weekly SLA compliance rate; every notice tracked to closure. Duration: 30 minutes agent time daily; more per active grievance.

PROD-W01Screen and validate a new product candidateon demand | scheduled weekly (bank sweep) · 8 steps

    Pull back once organic picks up

    Pull back ad spend for a SKU once its organic search ranking improves.

    prod/quick-commerce-ops
    Out adjusted ad spendCheck the pullback is triggered by a real organic-rank change, not a schedule
  3. 3
    Recompute ROAS from transaction value

    Recompute ROAS from transaction value, not the platform's MRP-based default, before judging spend.

    prod/quick-commerce-opsscript: metric contract
    Out recomputed ROASCheck the recompute uses transaction value, never the platform's MRP default
  4. 4
    Negotiate peak promotional windows

    Negotiate peak promotional windows (BFCM, Prime Day, Q4 holidays; india: festive windows) ahead of the calendar date.

    prod/quick-commerce-ops
    Out negotiated promo termsCheck negotiation happens ahead of the date, not during the window
  5. 5
    Watch dark-store stock daily

    Watch stock levels across the dark-store network daily, the way a merchandiser watches shelf stock.

    prod/quick-commerce-ops
    Out dark-store stock reportCheck the report covers every dark store the brand is live in
  6. 6
    Flag stockouts before the penalty

    Flag a dark-store stockout before it triggers an algorithmic ranking penalty.

    prod/quick-commerce-ops
    Out stockout flagCheck the flag fires before the platform's own ranking-penalty window closes
  7. 7
    Log the week

    Log ad spend, promo commitments and fill-rate flags to the registry.

    shared/registry-entry
    Out logged quick commerce ops recordCheck the log is comparable week over week

Outputs: ad credit spend log, promo calendar commitments, dark-store fill-rate flag. QA before the gate: ROAS recomputed from transaction value, not MRP; fill-rate flag raised before the ranking penalty window closes. Read point: weekly ad spend efficiency; daily fill-rate status. Duration: agent time under 1 hour daily for fill rate; 1 to 2 hours weekly for ad/promo.

PROD-W30Track regulatory registers: FDA, net-quantity, state licence and EPRmonthly audit, and on any formula/price change (india: MRP/GST change) | quarterly, annual filing deadline · 8 steps

As a person would call it: Compliance coordinator keeping every registration and filing current. Needs: SKU list with category, current FDA/state licence status (india: Legal Metrology and FSSAI licence status), state EPR registration status (india: EPR plastic-packaging registration status), relabelling requirements. Capabilities: PROD-C61, PROD-C62.

  1. 1
    Keep the licence register

    Keep one register of which SKUs need FDA facility registration or a state cosmetics/food/supplement licence (india: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) registration or an FSSAI licence; markets: IN).

    prod/regulatory-register-track
    Out licence registerCheck every SKU in a regulated category appears in the register
  2. 2
    Track validity windows

    Track each licence's current validity window.

    prod/regulatory-register-track
    Out validity window trackerCheck every licence's expiry date is current, not assumed
  3. 3
    Flag relabelling on formula/price change

    Flag the relabelling needed on any formula, claim or price change (india: any MRP or GST change; markets: IN).

    prod/regulatory-register-track
    Out relabelling flagCheck a flag is raised on every formula/claim/price change, not only at renewal (india: MRP or GST change; markets: IN)
  4. 4
    Register state EPR packaging

    Register the brand's packaging under the relevant state's EPR rules (india: India's EPR rules; markets: IN).

    prod/regulatory-register-track
    Out EPR registration statusCheck the registration covers every plastic packaging type the brand uses
  5. 5
    Track the annual EPR filing

    Track the annual EPR filing and recycling-target obligation.

    prod/regulatory-register-track
    Out EPR filing trackerCheck the filing deadline is tracked with enough lead time to act
  6. 6
    Flag a shortfall

    Flag when a shortfall means buying EPR credits.

    prod/regulatory-register-track
    Out EPR shortfall flagCheck the flag states the shortfall amount, not just that one exists
  7. 7
    Send expiring licences to the founder

    Send any licence expiring within 60 days to the founder gate.

    shared/plain-english-card
    Out founder cardCheck the card is sent with at least 60 days of lead time
  8. 8
    Log every filing

    Log every registration, filing and renewal to the registry.

    shared/registry-entry
    Out logged compliance recordCheck the log is the single source of truth for every SKU's compliance status

Outputs: compliance register, relabelling flag, EPR filing status. QA before the gate: every licence's validity window tracked, not assumed current; relabelling flagged on every formula/claim/price change, not just renewal (india: MRP/GST change; markets: IN). Read point: each licence's renewal date; the annual EPR filing deadline. Duration: agent time 1 to 2 hours monthly; quarterly EPR filing adds a few hours.

Money and ops MONEY · 24 workflows

MONEY-W01Month-end close: settlement reconciliation and management accountsmonthly, on the close calendar date | event: a settlement cycle ends · 13 steps

As a person would call it: the bookkeeper closing the month. Needs: brand brain: chart of accounts and cost classification tree, accounting export for the month, gateway settlement files, marketplace settlement files, India only: COD courier remittance files, open dispute list, fixed asset register, last month's P&L ladder. Capabilities: MONEY-C01, MONEY-C15, MONEY-C51, MONEY-C52, MONEY-C56, MONEY-C60, MONEY-G01, MONEY-G05.

  1. 1
    Pull the month's raw exports

    Pull Shopify and marketplace orders, gateway settlement files, the accounting export for the close month, and, for an India-selling brand, courier COD remittance files.

    no skill, judgementconnector: shopify orders (read)connector: accounting export (read)connector: marketplace settlement (read)connector: courier COD remittance (read, India only)
    Out raw export set with row counts per sourceCheck every source file is present and dated inside the close monthAsk founder if a source connector has no read access yet
  2. 2
    Reconcile the gateway settlement

    Unbundle each gateway payout into gross sale, fee, refund, sales tax withheld on the fee (GST on the fee for India-selling brands) and net, then match it to the bank credit.

    money/reconcile/gatewayscript: money.reconciliation
    Out gateway reconciliation table with a named cause per gapCheck every payout ties to a bank credit within 2 days or is flagged aged
  3. 3
    Reconcile marketplace settlements

    Unbundle commission, fixed fee, shipping fee, marketplace-facilitator sales tax withheld, 1099-K totals and refunds for each marketplace payout. India-selling brands unbundle TCS under Section 52 and GST on fees the same way, as a market option.

    money/reconcile/marketplacescript: money.reconciliation
    Out marketplace reconciliation table, one row per payoutCheck facilitator sales tax (or TCS/GST for India) and fees are broken out on their own lines, never netted into one number
  4. 4
    India only: reconcile COD cash and courier remittance

    For an India-selling brand running COD, age cash collected by each courier against what has actually reached the bank, by courier. Reads null for US-only brands, whose payout reconciliation is fully covered by steps 2 and 3.

    money/reconcile/cod-courierscript: money.reconciliation
    Out COD aging table by courierCheck every remittance stuck past the courier's own SLA cycle is flagged with an escalation note and a named contact
  5. 5
    Reconcile ad platform invoices to logged spend

    Match the Meta and Google invoice amounts for the month to the spend the dashboards report.

    money/reconcile/ad-platform-invoicesscript: money.reconciliationmcp: Meta_MCP ads_get_dataset_stats
    Out ad spend reconciliation line with varianceCheck any gap over 1 percent has a named cause, never left as rounding
  6. 6
    Build the evidence pack for each open dispute

    Assemble the order record, delivery proof, verification log and support chat for each open chargeback or dispute (Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal; UPI dispute for India-selling brands), and check its filing deadline.

    money/reconcile/chargebacksscript: money.reconciliationconnector: shopify orders (read)
    Out one evidence pack per open dispute, with a filing deadlineCheck no dispute is missing its filing deadlineAsk founder if a dispute needs a person to submit it through the gateway's own portal
  7. 7
    Update the fixed asset register

    Log any new capital purchase this month (equipment, fixtures, website build cost, packaging dies) and run the depreciation schedule.

    money/fixed-asset-registerscript: money.fixed_asset_depreciation
    Out updated register with this month's depreciation lineCheck every asset carries purchase date, useful life and a running balance
  8. 8
    Run the cost classification and P&L ladder

    Apply the fixed decision tree for COGS, cost of delivery, marketing cost and OPEX, and build the ladder from gross revenue to net profit.

    money/pnl-close-checklistscript: money.pnl_ladder
    Out P&L ladder for the monthCheck every line traces to a source; no line is double-counted between COGS and OPEX
  9. 9
    Draft the settlement journal entries

    Draft one journal entry per settlement from the unbundled lines, instead of one lump bank deposit.

    money/reconcile/gatewayscript: money.reconciliationconnector: accounting export (read)
    Out draft journal entries for the accountant to postCheck each entry's lines sum exactly to its bank credit
  10. 10
    Run the close checklist

    Run bank reconciliations, accrual review, inventory valuation and deferred revenue checks.

    money/pnl-close-checklistscript: money.pnl_ladder
    Out close checklist, pass or fail per itemCheck no open item is left without an owner and a target date
  11. 11
    Diff against last month

    Compare the ladder and every reconciliation line to the prior month and name the single biggest change.

    shared/metric-readscript: money.pnl_ladder
    Out one paragraph naming the biggest change and its causeCheck the paragraph names a cause, not only a number
  12. 12
    Publish the management accounts

    Package the ladder, the reconciliation bridge and dispute status into the monthly management accounts report.

    shared/report-sectionscript: money.pnl_ladder
    Out management accounts reportCheck every number carries a source and a freshness stamp
  13. 13
    Route unresolved items

    Send anything needing a signature, a gateway portal action or a judgment call outside the cost tree to the founder or bookkeeper.

    shared/plain-english-card
    Out routed action list with ownersCheck every unresolved item has a named owner and a dateAsk founder if an accrual judgment call is not covered by the current cost classification tree

Outputs: P&L ladder, reconciliation bridge (gateway, marketplace, ad invoices, chargebacks, and COD for India-selling brands), dispute evidence packs, fixed asset register update, management accounts report, close checklist. QA before the gate: every number sourced and freshness stamped; no missing value shown as zero; no ad account write attempted; facilitator sales tax (or GST and TCS for India) never netted into one line. Read point: on publish, against last month's ladder and the annual budget. Duration: agent: 2 to 3 hours across the steps; waiting: up to 2 days for settlement files and accountant sign-off.

MONEY-W02Weekly contribution margin, SKU and customer profitabilityweekly (margin, SKU) | quarterly (customer profitability, or before a loyalty tier redesign) · 8 steps

As a person would call it: the finance analyst running the margin report. Needs: brand brain: SKU cost lines, product/SKU list, order export with channel and basket detail, support ticket cost per contact, return and refund log, discount ledger, prior period's margin table. Capabilities: MONEY-C02, MONEY-C17, LIFE-C62.

  1. 1
    Pull orders, costs and support cost

    Pull the week's orders with SKU, basket and channel detail, landed cost per SKU, support ticket cost, return cost and discount cost.

    no skill, judgementconnector: shopify orders (read)connector: accounting export (read)
    Out joined order-cost datasetCheck every order has a channel tag and every SKU has a landed cost
  2. 2
    Compute CM1, CM2 and CM3

    Compute CM1 (after COGS), CM2 (after delivery cost) and CM3 (after marketing cost), each labeled by scope.

    money/marginscript: money.contribution_margin
    Out CM1/CM2/CM3 by basket, SKU and channelCheck no margin number is shown without its scope label
  3. 3
    Classify each SKU

    Classify every SKU as champion, hidden gem, growth driver or underperformer on contribution and cash tied up.

    money/marginscript: money.sku_matrix
    Out ranked SKU contribution table with a classification tagCheck every SKU has exactly one classification
  4. 4
    Flag rationalization candidates

    Flag SKUs that are both cash-heavy and low-contribution for rationalization review.

    money/marginscript: money.sku_matrix
    Out rationalization candidate listCheck each candidate lists its contribution, cash tied up and last-90-day sell-through
  5. 5
    Add support, return and discount cost per customer

    Add support-ticket cost, return and refund cost, shipping cost and discount cost against each customer's revenue, in code.

    money/margin/customer-profitabilityscript: money.customer_profitability
    Out true customer profitability tableCheck no cost bucket is estimated; a missing bucket shows as unavailable
  6. 6
    Feed loyalty tiering

    Rank customers by true profitability, not revenue, and flag mismatches against the current loyalty tier.

    money/margin/customer-profitabilityscript: money.customer_profitability
    Out tier-mismatch listCheck every flagged customer shows the gap between tier and true profitabilityAsk founder if a tier redesign would move a named VIP customer down
  7. 7
    Diff against the prior period

    Compare this period's CM, SKU classifications and customer profitability to the last run.

    shared/metric-readscript: money.contribution_margin
    Out change list since last runCheck every named change states the driver, not just the delta
  8. 8
    Publish the standing report

    Publish the CM, SKU and customer profitability report so nobody guesses what a margin number includes.

    shared/report-section
    Out contribution margin and profitability reportCheck every figure states CM1, CM2 or CM3 explicitly

Outputs: CM1/CM2/CM3 report, SKU contribution and classification table, customer profitability table, rationalization candidate list. QA before the gate: margin scope always labeled; no revenue shown where profit was asked for; missing cost bucket shown as unavailable, not zero. Read point: weekly for CM and SKU; quarterly for customer profitability, against the prior run. Duration: agent: 45 to 90 minutes; no material waiting time.

MONEY-W03Price and promo economics gateevent: new SKU or cost change | event: a promo is proposed · 7 steps

As a person would call it: the founder's pricing and promotions check. Needs: brand brain: net-profit target, landed cost, proposed price or promo terms, 90-day sales history for the SKU, metric contract: current CM by SKU. Capabilities: MONEY-C04, MONEY-C05.

  1. 1
    Take the net-profit target

    Read the brand's net-profit target for the SKU or line, never a keystone rule of thumb.

    no skill, judgement
    Out target net-profit percentCheck the target came from the brand brain, not an assumed default
  2. 2
    Solve the price waterfall

    Solve bottom-up from landed cost through fees, shipping, returns and marketing cost to the shelf price that hits the target.

    money/pricing-waterfallscript: money.pricing_waterfall
    Out proposed shelf price with full waterfallCheck the waterfall shows every line between cost and price, none skipped
  3. 3
    Or model the promo economics

    For a proposed promo (percent-off, BOGO, gift-with-purchase, flash sale), model its real cost shape through the same waterfall.

    money/pricing-waterfallscript: money.promo_breakeven
    Out promo cost modelCheck the model uses the promo's real mechanic, not a flat percent-off assumption
  4. 4
    Run the break-even check

    Run a break-even go/no-go check on the promo, or a margin stress-test on the new price.

    money/pricing-waterfallscript: money.promo_breakeven
    Out go/no-go recommendation with the break-even volumeCheck the recommendation states the exact volume or margin needed to break even
  5. 5
    Stress-test 60 to 90 days out

    For a new price, stress-test it against 60 to 90 days of actual sell-through once live.

    money/pricing-waterfallscript: money.pricing_waterfall
    Out stress-test noteCheck the stress-test uses real sell-through, not the launch-day forecast
  6. 6
    Write the founder brief

    Write the recommendation, the numbers behind it and the risk, with an explicit approve, reject or park line.

    shared/developer-brief
    Out founder brief with approve/reject/park lineCheck the brief states the number the founder is approving, not just a description
  7. 7
    Stop for approval

    Stop before the price or promo goes public. Do not draft the site or ad copy change until approved.

    shared/founder-question-round
    Out approval recordCheck no downstream artefact is drafted before this step returns approvedAsk founder if always: this capability is founder_gate

Outputs: price waterfall, promo break-even model, founder brief with approve/reject/park line. QA before the gate: profit target never replaced by keystone; sales-tax (or TCS/GST for India) and fee lines all present in the waterfall; no live change without recorded approval. Read point: 60 to 90 days after a price goes live, or the day after a promo ends. Duration: agent: 30 to 60 minutes; waiting: founder decision turnaround.

MONEY-W04Cash forecast, inventory planning and financing evaluationweekly (forecast, inventory) | on demand (financing evaluation) · 9 steps

As a person would call it: the person planning cash for the next quarter. Needs: brand brain: bank balance, payroll calendar, supplier lead times, ad spend plan, inventory on order, current financing terms if any. Capabilities: MONEY-C06, MONEY-C07, MONEY-C08, PROD-C42.

  1. 1
    Pull cash inputs

    Pull the bank balance, payroll calendar, supplier lead times, inventory on order and the ad spend plan.

    no skill, judgementconnector: accounting export (read)
    Out cash input setCheck all five inputs present or named as unavailable
  2. 2
    Build the 13-week forecast

    Build a rolling 13-week cash forecast from the inputs.

    money/cash-forecast-13wkscript: money.cash_forecast_13wk
    Out 13-week cash tableCheck the forecast never lets inventory cash go negative
  3. 3
    Reconcile profit to free cash flow

    Reconcile this month's profit to free cash flow and name the gap.

    money/cash-forecast-13wkscript: money.cash_forecast_13wk
    Out profit-to-cash bridgeCheck the bridge names each of the 4 hidden cash traps checked
  4. 4
    Flag the lowest cash point

    Flag the lowest projected cash week before it happens, with a sensitivity range.

    money/cash-forecast-13wkscript: money.cash_forecast_13wk
    Out lowest-cash-week flag with sensitivity noteCheck the flag fires at least 3 weeks before the low point
  5. 5
    Roll inventory cash forward

    Roll inventory forward with lead time to plan cash, targeting days-of-inventory to supplier lead time.

    money/cash-forecast-13wkscript: money.cash_forecast_13wk
    Out inventory cash planCheck days-of-inventory is compared to lead time explicitly, not left implicit
  6. 6
    Manage the cash conversion cycle

    Track days inventory, days payable and days receivable together as the cash conversion cycle.

    money/cash-forecast-13wkscript: money.cash_forecast_13wk
    Out cash conversion cycle number with trendCheck the cycle is shown as one number with its 3 parts, not only the parts
  7. 7
    Compare financing options

    When cash runs low or a hard-to-source launch needs funding, compare real borrowing options (line of credit, inventory financing, revenue-based) and, for a hard-to-fund launch, crowdfunding, private capital or manufacturer referrals, against reference cost-of-capital rates.

    money/financing-comparisonweb: search (public, budgeted)
    Out financing option comparisonCheck every option shows its real cost of capital, not the advertised rate
  8. 8
    Stress-test repayments

    Stress-test any financing option's repayment schedule against a slower-sales scenario.

    money/financing-comparisonscript: money.cash_forecast_13wk
    Out repayment stress-testCheck the stress case uses the brand's own slow-month history, not a generic haircut
  9. 9
    Write the founder brief and stop

    Write the recommendation and stop for approval before any financing commitment or launch spend is signed.

    shared/developer-brief
    Out founder brief with approve/reject/park lineCheck no financing or sourcing commitment is treated as decided by this agentAsk founder if always: financing evaluation and sourcing decisions are human_assist

Outputs: 13-week cash forecast, inventory cash plan, financing option comparison, founder brief. QA before the gate: inventory never modeled negative; profit and cash reconciled monthly; financing cost shown at its real rate. Read point: weekly against the rolling forecast; on demand when financing is evaluated. Duration: agent: 1 to 2 hours; waiting: lender or manufacturer response time for financing evaluation.

MONEY-W05Capital raising, investor and lender reporting, and insuranceon demand (raise or loan process) | monthly (reporting) | quarterly (board deck) | annually (insurance renewal) | event: insured loss · 7 steps

As a person would call it: the person assembling the data room and the cover. Needs: brand brain: cap table, prior raises, insurance policies, P&L ladder, cash forecast, CAC/LTV report, loss or claim event details. Capabilities: MONEY-C58, MONEY-C59, MONEY-G02.

  3. 3

MONEY-W06Report unit economics and plan the growth budgetweekly (CAC, LTV, revenue forecast) | monthly (OPEX budget, MMM refresh) · 10 steps

As a person would call it: the growth finance lead. Needs: metric contract: CAC bands, orders with cohort and channel tags, ad spend by channel, marketing calendar, subscription plan terms if any, prior period's forecast. Capabilities: MONEY-C09, MONEY-C10, MONEY-C11, MONEY-C18, MONEY-C63.

    Screen the order set for fraud and bot-driven orders before computing any cohort number.

    money/growth-economics-stackscript: money.cac_ltv_cohorts

  2. 2
    Compute the 4 labeled CACs

    Compute blended, media-only, paid and fully loaded CAC from spend and orders.

    money/growth-economics-stackscript: money.cac_ltv_cohorts

  3. 3

  4. 4

    money/growth-economics-stackscript: money.cac_ltv_cohorts
    Out scale/hold recommendationCheck the recommendation names the cohort it is based on

    Build subscription unit economics

    If the brand has subscriptions, build churn against the correct prior-period base, conservative lifetime estimates, and prepaid-plan economics.

    money/growth-economics-stackscript: money.subscription_economics

    Build the annual budget

    Build the annual budget separate from the rolling forecast, sizing OPEX and payroll to the brand's own profit target.

  8. 8
    Answer the marginal spend question

    Answer marginal spend questions (the next 10,000 dollars) by ranking channels on CM3 and CAC payback.

MONEY-W07US sales tax nexus, filing and marketplace-facilitator compliance trackingmonthly, before the state sales-tax filing deadline (India: before GST return filing) | event: new SKU or B2B dispatch · 8 steps

As a person would call it: the person tracking sales-tax and marketplace compliance. Needs: brand brain: selling markets, SKU list, registered states, Avalara or TaxJar taxability and filing status, return and refund log, credit memo register, gift card and loyalty point ledger, India only: GSTR-2B, stock transfer and B2B dispatch log. Capabilities: MONEY-C12, MONEY-G04, LIFE-C55, PROD-C60.

  1. 1
    Assign and validate product tax codes

    Build and keep the SKU-to-product-tax-code map correct in Avalara or TaxJar for every SKU, since a wrong or missing code is a common cause of miscollected sales tax. India-selling brands keep the same SKU-to-HSN/SAC map, as a market option, since a wrong or too-short HSN/SAC code is a common cause of e-invoice portal rejections.

    money/gst-tax-compliancescript: money.hsn_map_validate
    Out SKU-to-product-tax-code map (India: SKU-to-HSN/SAC map)Check no SKU ships without a validated code
  2. 2
    Track sales-tax nexus and registration thresholds

    Track economic-nexus and registration thresholds per state the brand sells into (India-selling brands track GST nexus and registration thresholds the same way, as a market option).

    money/gst-tax-compliancescript: money.compliance_tracker
    Out nexus and threshold status by marketCheck a market crossing a threshold is flagged before the filing deadline, not after
  3. 3
    Prepare state sales-tax filing inputs

    Prepare the return-ready sales and exemption data each registered state's filing needs, from Avalara or TaxJar. India-selling brands prepare the sales and input-credit data GSTR-1 and 3B need, and match input credit against GSTR-2B, as a market option.

    money/gst-tax-compliancescript: money.compliance_tracker
    Out state filing input pack (India: GSTR-1/3B input pack)Check every mismatch between claimed and available credit is listed, not netted away
  4. 4
    Reconcile marketplace facilitator sales tax and 1099-K

    Reconcile sales tax collected and remitted by each marketplace as facilitator against the credit or exclusion the brand can actually claim, and match 1099-K gross totals to the ledger. Brand strategist BRAND · 30 workflows

BRAND-W01Run the customer research sweepscheduled monthly | on demand before an avatar or positioning refresh · 8 steps

As a person would call it: what a customer insights analyst does at the start of every research cycle. Needs: brand brain: product list and SKUs, connector: reviews export (site + marketplace), connector: support desk export (tickets, returns, calls), connector: GA4 / on-site search log, budget ledger: remaining balance for any paid deep-research pass.   1. 1
    Pull and tag reviews by star band

As a person would call it: what a founder or researcher does to hear the job in the customer's own words. Needs: research packet from BRAND-W01, customer list or panel access, founder availability for the incentive decision. Capabilities: BRAND-C05.

  3. 3

    no skill, judgement
    Out scheduled interviews or handoff noteCheck every scheduled interview has a guide attachedAsk founder if no one is available to run the conversations this cycle

  8. 8

Outputs: interview guide, transcript log, interview findings packet. QA before the gate: every question is open, not leading; every transcript has a consent flag; incentive cost computed, not guessed. Read point: not a metric read; a qualitative evidence build feeding the next avatar cycle.. Duration: agent time 3-5 hours to prepare and synthesize; 1-3 weeks wait for scheduling and running 8-12 conversations..

BRAND-W03Design and field a customer surveyquarterly | on demand to confirm a research finding at scale · 7 steps

As a person would call it: what a researcher does to check a finding against the wider customer base, never to discover a new job.   2. 2

Outputs: survey question set, cleaned response set, confirm/deny result. QA before the gate: 6 questions or fewer; survey confirms an existing finding, never fishes for a new one; send only after founder approval. Read point: scored the day the response window closes, with sample size reported.. Duration: agent time 2-3 hours to design and score; 1-2 weeks wait for the response window..

BRAND-W05Build and gate a new avatar recordevent: a new avatar is needed, or the quarterly recheck finds the current one stale · 9 steps

As a person would call it: what a brand strategist does to turn scattered research into one usable customer record. Needs: research packet from BRAND-W01 (and W02/W03 if run), competitor packet from BRAND-W04 if positioning-relevant, founder sign-off on which candidate to build. Capabilities: BRAND-C09, BRAND-C13, BRAND-C11.

Outputs: job statement, objection map, 5W profile, full avatar record, registry entry.     Search the USPTO trademark database and international equivalents, check name + industry-term collisions, check domain and social handle availability, and check meaning and sound in relevant languages (Spanish for US customers, plus Hindi or any other export-market language when the brand sells into that market).

    brand/trademark-domain-checkscript: domain_checkerweb search
    Out clearance report per finalistCheck every finalist has a status: clear, risk, or needs-legalAsk founder if a finalist needs a paid legal opinion or filing
  6. 6

  7. 7
    Write the short story and tagline (full brand names only)

    brand/name-screening-and-packagingscript: naming_deliverable_builderscript: strip_test
    Out naming deliverableCheck tagline fails the strip test if a competitor's name could swap in and it would still read true
  8. 8

Outputs: raw candidate list, scored shortlist, clearance report, naming deliverable or SKU name. Read point: not a metric read; naming is a one-time deliverable per project.. Duration: agent time 1-2 days for a full brand name; 1-2 hours for a SKU/collection name; legal clearance can add 1-2 weeks if a paid opinion is needed..

BRAND-W13Decide brand architecture for a new line or marketevent: a new product line, category extension or market entry is proposed · 7 steps

As a person would call it: what a brand architect decides before a new line ships under a name. Needs: proposed new line or market, current brand equity and guidelines, avatar overlap between current brand and the new line's likely buyer. Capabilities: BRAND-C30.

  1. 1
    Run the teeter-totter test

    Check whether the new line would pull equity away from the parent brand's core meaning if given the master brand name (does adding this make the master brand mean less, not more).

  2. 2
    Run the shopping-list test

    Check whether a shopper would naturally put the new line on the same mental shopping list as the current brand, or whether it reads as a different errand entirely.

    no skill, judgement
    Out shopping-list verdictCheck verdict names the specific shopper behavior it is based on
  3. 3
    Check avatar overlap

    Compare the new line's likely buyer against the current primary avatar for real overlap, not assumed overlap.

    no skill, judgement
    Out overlap readCheck overlap stated as high, partial or low, with the evidence
  4. 4
    Default to one master brand for a small brand

    Unless a real reason surfaces in steps 1-3 (equity dilution risk, no shopping-list overlap, real reputational separation needed), recommend the master-brand name over a new name, since a small brand cannot afford to build two names.

    no skill, judgementscript: brand_architecture_checklist
    Out architecture recommendation (master brand vs new name)Check a 'new name' recommendation must name the specific reason the default was overridden
  5. 5
    Route naming if a new name is warranted

    If a new name is recommended, hand off to BRAND-W12 for the naming project.

    no skill, judgement

    Founder gate

    Present the recommendation and reasoning to the founder.

    shared/founder-question-roundshared/plain-english-card
    Out founder decisionCheck card states the default and why it was or was not overriddenAsk founder if always
  7. 7
    Log the decision

    Write the decision and reasoning to the registry and brand brain.

    shared/registry-entryscript: brand_brain_writer
    Out registry entry, brand brain updateCheck reasoning is kept, not just the yes/no outcome

Outputs: teeter-totter verdict, shopping-list verdict, architecture recommendation, registry entry. QA before the gate: default to one master brand unless a named reason overrides it; every verdict is a specific mechanism, not a feeling. Read point: not a metric read; a one-time architecture decision per new line or market.. Duration: agent time 2-3 hours; founder review 1-3 days..

BRAND-W14Draft the brand story, voice sheet and promiseon demand | event: new brand, voice drift found, or a new promise/tagline is needed · 9 steps

  8. 8

BRAND-W17Audit brand consistency and diagnose the perception gapscheduled monthly (consistency) | quarterly, run together with the perception-gap pass · 8 steps

As a person would call it: what a brand manager does walking the live brand against its own rulebook, then checking the rulebook against reality. Outputs: site drift list, ads/email drift list, perception-gap note, fix list. Skill tree

Skills nest. The agent picks by the task's switches.

A parent skill holds sub-skills selected by format, channel, platform, flow type, marketplace or supplier region. Each has a SKILL.md with purpose, inputs, steps, checks and an example. Shared skills live in agents/skills and any agent may call them.

owner: site-specialist
version: 1
invoke_when: any store setup or configuration task in 05-SET (platform choice, foundation, domain, catalogue, architecture, markets, consent)

# Store setup checklist

## Purpose
Turn a setup or configuration task into an evidence-based pass/fail list instead of a settings-page glance, so nothing is marked done without being read.

## Steps
1. Pull the idea-bank items and required-state rules for the section in question.
2. Read the live configuration through the platform connector (Shopify Admin, WooCommerce REST API).
3. Compare live state to required state, one field or setting at a time.
4. For every fail, write down the exact evidence (the value read, the value required).
5. Write the fix, sized to whether a person or the founder needs to act.
6. Mark pass only where a live read confirmed it.

## Checks
- No item marked pass from memory or a settings screenshot alone.
- Every fail has a concrete, actionable fix.
- Evidence is dated so staleness is visible later.

## Output
A checklist table plus a one-line summary a founder can read in 10 seconds.

## Example
"Payment capture timing: FAIL. Live value: manual capture. Required: automatic within 3 days. Fix: change capture setting in Shopify Payments settings, 2 minutes, no dependency."

# Payments, shipping and tax setup

## Purpose
Configure the 3 setup areas where a wrong number costs real money on day one, and prove every one of them with a real test, not a settings screenshot.

## Steps
1. For payments: verify identity documents exactly, add a second gateway (Shop Pay, PayPal, Apple Pay, a BNPL option such as Affirm, Klarna or Afterpay) and regional methods, set capture and fraud rules.
2. Test every gateway in sandbox, then place and refund one real order before removing the storefront password.
3. For shipping: build zones so every country has an explicit rate, set the free-shipping threshold from real margin and AOV.
4. Test every rate bracket at its edge with a real cart.
5. For tax: confirm real obligations with a professional first, then enable the calculation service per jurisdiction (state nexus and marketplace facilitator rules for the US).
6. Decide inclusive/exclusive display and tax basis per jurisdiction's real rule, and test one product per tax class in 2+ regions.

## Checks
- A real refunded order exists in the gateway dashboard.
- Every shipping bracket boundary was tested with a real cart.
- No tax jurisdiction configured without a professional's sign-off on file.

## Output
One configuration + test log per area, each line naming the setting, the value, the test performed and the result.

## Example
"Free shipping threshold: set at $59, from AOV $46 and 42% margin. Tested at $58.99 (rate shown) and $59.00 (free), both correct."

# Pre-launch QA and launch sequencing

## Purpose
Prove, with real customer actions, that a store is actually ready to sell, and give one clear go or no-go call before the password comes off.

## Steps
1. Pull every prior setup workflow's result into one dependency-ordered list.
2. For each line, perform the real action a customer would take (browse, add to cart, pay, receive an email) rather than checking a setting.
3. Run a full mobile QA pass across the brand's real device split.
4. Check the logged-out storefront in an incognito window, clicking every visible element.
5. Compile the pass/fail table.
6. Give one clear go or no-go call, naming any blocking failure.
7. Remove the storefront password only once every line passes.

## Checks
- Every line closed with a real action, not an admin-panel glance.
- No password removal before 100% pass.
- The go/no-go call is unambiguous.

## Output
A pass/fail table plus a one-line go/no-go recommendation with any blocker named.

## Example
"38 of 38 checks pass. Go. Password removed 14:02 IST, confirmed by a live incognito purchase test immediately after."

# Post-launch hygiene sweep

## Purpose
Catch the small things quietly going wrong on a live store before they become a support flood or a lost sale, on a fixed weekly cadence.

## Steps
1. Reconcile platform inventory against real stock (weekly for month one, then as risk warrants).
2. Classify support tickets by root cause; anything outside Site's 4 folders gets routed with site/handoff-note, not dropped.
3. Re-run shipping and tax checks whenever a product, zone or app changed this week.
4. Confirm review-request automation and the payout bank account are both actually working, checked against a real order.
5. Sweep for broken links to images, CSS and JS, and collapse any redirect chain to one 301.

## Checks
- Every recurring ticket cluster maps to a named root cause or is routed to the right specialist.
- No item marked fixed without a live re-check.

## Output
A short weekly hygiene report and a fix list, each fix naming who does it.

## Example
"Ticket cluster (11 this week): 'where is my size chart' on the linen shirt PDP. Root cause: size chart missing after last theme update. Fix: re-add via SITE-W11, same day."

# Theme engineering practice

## Purpose
Pick a theme on real fit, not a demo, and keep every later change consistent with one documented set of design tokens instead of drifting section by section.

## Steps
1. Write the required feature and section list before opening any theme.
2. Vet each candidate on a real product page and a real mobile width, not the homepage demo.
3. Score candidates against the list, note the runner-up and why it lost.
4. Once a theme is live, document its color, spacing, typography and component tokens.
5. Check every new homepage or PDP section, native or page-builder, against the token set.
6. Flag any drift (wrong radius, font size, spacing) before the section ships.

## Checks
- Vetting happened on PDP and mobile, never the homepage demo alone.
- Every new section was checked against the token doc, not shipped by eye.

## Output
A scored theme shortlist for a selection task, or a token doc plus drift flags for an ongoing design-system check.

## Example
"New FAQ accordion built in Replo used a 6px border radius; brand token is 4px. Flagged and corrected before publish."

# AI build-agent guardrail

## Purpose
Keep an AI coding agent's storefront work safe and reviewable: real inputs, one change at a time, private preview, and manual QA before anything the agent wrote reaches a customer.

## Steps
1. Write a brief with the real product, policy and voice inputs the agent needs; never send it in with a bare one-line prompt.
2. Let the agent interview and propose a plan before it starts building.
3. Ask for exactly one storefront change per prompt, and verify each one live before the next.
4. Preview every change privately; never let the agent's output reach the public URL directly.
5. Treat the AI-authored section as a draft: run mobile QA and a claims check (shared/claim-check) on it.
6. Plan long sessions around a possible usage-limit pause so a half-finished change isn't left live.

## Checks
- Every AI-authored section passed a claim check before merge.
- No public URL ever served an unreviewed AI change.

## Output
The AI build brief used to start the session, a QA pass report, and a change log entry per shipped edit.

## Example
"Brief: rebuild the size-chart tab using the real size data in brand.json. Agent proposed a plan, built on a duplicate theme, previewed privately, claim-check passed, merged via reviewed PR."
